newsitem.title: HONG KONG: People leap from windows in HK blaze, fireman killed.
newsitem.headline: People leap from windows in HK blaze, fireman killed.

text.p: People leapt from windows or clung by their fingertips to air conditioners on exterior walls to escape a fire in a Hong Kong commercial high-rise building on Wednesday, and one fireman was killed battling the blaze.

A dramatic rescue operation was launched by 160 Hong Kong firefighters to save scores of people who got trapped in the 16-floor building on the bustling Nathan Road, heart of the Kowloon tourist shopping district.
Terrified people jumped from window ledges on to rescue ladders and others scrambled on to ledges and air conditioners. A few were winched off the building by helicopter.
As many as 68 people were injured in the disaster, including two firefighters, one of whom later died of injuries suffered when he fell down the building's lift shaft, officials said.
A fireman said the inferno appeared to have begun on the ground floor, where a China arts and crafts store is located.
The blaze engulfed the first four storeys of the building, as well as the top three floors after spreading upwards through the elevator shaft, government-run Hong Kong radio said.
The fire sent up high flames and spewed a darkening cloud over the Kowloon peninsula. The cause of the fire was not clear.
Most of the injured suffered from smoke inhalation.
After four hours the government's security chief Peter lai said rescue services were bringing the fire under control.
"According to the commander at the scene, the fire started at the ground floor at the lift area and spread very quickly," Lai told reporters.
"We believe all those who were trapped have been rescued. But that cannot possibly be confirmed yet. The fire is basically under control," Lai said.
As the top floor still burned late in the evening, firefighters were combing the building floor by floor to check for any more trapped or injured people, he said.

One eyewitness said she had seen a man plunge from the building in the rush to escape. "I saw him climb from the window and cling to an air conditioner, then the airconditioner fell and he fell too," a resident in a flat across the road said.
